subject: zenGarden
pitch: A small Japanese garden diorama on a square base. A curved red wooden bridge over a koi pond with three orange and white koi, a stone lantern, a little pine tree with cloud-shaped foliage, a cherry tree in full pink blossom dropping petals, raked white gravel with a few mossy rocks, and stepping stones leading to the bridge.
reasoning:
Since there's no creature in this scene, I'm planning the diorama as a set of simple props built through the same builder structure, starting with a root joint and laying out a base platform roughly a meter square with a slightly raised top surface around 0.06-0.08m high.

Now I'm working out the zone layout: a pond off-center-left shaped as a flattened wide cylinder sitting just above the ground to hide its edge with a ring of rim stones, a raked gravel area in the lighter back-right, and a bridge spanning across the pond along the x-axis with stepping stones leading toward it from the front.

I'm placing the remaining elements -- stepping stones trailing from the front-right corner toward the bridge, a stone lantern and cherry tree tucked into the back-left, and a pine tree on the grass near the front-left, while deciding where gravel versus grass patches should border each feature.

For the koi, I'll give each fish a simple four-joint spine chain with swept body geometry, painted orange and white patches, and extruded fins, positioning three of them swimming in the pond at water level.

Each koi chain needs a root parent joint. Now I'm designing the bridge as a swept box section following an arched path, with the deck curving up from ground level on both ends using a parabolic height profile.

For the sweep orientation, since the path runs horizontally along x, I'm reasoning through how the local axes fall back to world up when the tangent is sideways, making sure the box width spans correctly across z while height stays vertical — I'll just pass an explicit up vector of [0,1,0] to keep it safe. Now I'm starting on the railing posts, placing them along the deck at intervals.

Computing plank rotation angles...

Now I'm adding stringer sweeps with dark coloring, then setting up a helper function to simplify placing parts with a shared root bone. Next I'm building the ground: a dark wood base box topped with a thinner grass layer.

Finishing the ground top height, I'm adding a mottled grass texture, then creating a small pond with a thin flattened cylinder of water surrounded by a ring of rocks along its elliptical bank.

I'm working out koi placement so they sit partly submerged, adjusting their size and vertical position so they peek just above the water surface without floating unnaturally high.

Adding ripple rings around the koi using flattened torus shapes, plus a few lily pads with pink flowers, then building the gravel bed with rake-line texture using thin boxes layered just above the gravel surface.

I'm also thinking about concentric ripple rings around two rocks instead of straight lines there, keeping straight rake lines for the rest of the gravel, and adding simple brown wood edging boxes around the border. Next I'll work on a function for the mossy rocks.

Still designing the lantern...

Now I'm sketching the pine tree: a curved brown trunk with tapering radii, three sprouting branches, and flattened foliage clusters made from blobby icosahedron shapes in shaded greens, plus a cherry tree nearby with a thick dark curved trunk.

For the cherry's canopy, I'm scattering pink blossom blobs across the branch tips in varied shades, then adding falling petals as tiny flat rotated shapes scattered both on the ground and floating in the air for a dynamic effect.

I'm keeping the total part count manageable around 300, placing the canopy clusters within a defined radius near the trunk, and now figuring out the koi positions within the pond.

Placing three koi at distinct spots inside the pond ellipse, checking each stays within bounds, and writing a helper function that computes each fish's body curve from its heading and bend direction...

Defining tapered spine points...

Still shaping the radius curve...

I'm also planning the color patches with orange and a darker rust tone scattered across the fish body, then moving on to extruding the tail fin outward.

Writing tail and pectoral fin geometry...

Adding the eye sphere, then setting up bone and helper functions for building parts, with a limited color palette to keep the design under budget.

I'm plotting the cherry tree trunk as a smoothed curved sweep with tapering radii embedded in the ground, then adding several branch sweeps extending outward and upward from different points along the trunk.

For the foliage, I'm scattering clusters of icosahedron blobs around the branch tips and trunk top in soft pink tones, varying sizes and offsets randomly for a natural look, with a few lighter blobs layered on top as highlights.

Now I'm switching to the pine tree, laying out its trunk path and radii, then defining cloud-pad side branches with clustered flattened icosahedron pads for the foliage shape.

I need to check the bounding box carefully -- the right pad extends past the 0.6 limit, so I'm shifting the trunk x-position to 0.42 and adjusting pad offsets to keep everything within bounds, while also verifying the gravel patch doesn't overlap the trunk base.

Now I'm placing the remaining elements: a rock near the pine, tightening the gravel patch dimensions, and checking the cherry tree, lantern, and pine positions all stay clear of each other. I'm also laying out the stepping stones leading toward the bridge's east end and confirming the pond's eastern edge doesn't collide with the stones.

Then I work out the bridge geometry — curved deck spanning from one grass edge to the other across the pond, using a parametric height curve that peaks in the middle, with plank thickness and post placement at the rails, plus small foot stones at each end for a clean landing.

Posts get small capped sphere tops with rail sweeps connecting them using catmull curves through the post points, colored in red and gold tones. I'm finalizing the palette and moving on to writing the actual rendering code now.

Writing wood base and pond layers...

Now I'm adding ripples around the koi using thin flattened tori near the water surface, plus lily pads as flattened green cylinders with small pink cone flowers scattered across the pond. Then I'm moving on to designing the lantern.

Adjusting the proportions...

Working out the platform, fire box, posts, roof cone, and top sphere stacking for the stone lantern, accepting the total height even though it's a bit tall relative to the bridge. Moving on to rock scaling parameters and petal randomization for the surrounding details.

Now I'm scattering ground-cover points, varying their height depending on whether they land on grass, water in the pond ellipse, gravel path, or the bridge footprint (which I skip to avoid overlap), plus adding a batch of falling elements near the tree.

Adding more rake lines and gravel edging...

Now placing scattered rocks near the cherry tree and lantern, plus a couple of round azalea bushes for greenery, then starting to think through the sweep function for the paths.

For the koi, I'm working out how to safely pass the bone parameter during the sweep, defaulting to root for stability, and planning a koi-generating function that uses heading, bend, and seed values to compute direction vectors for each fish's position and orientation.

Still writing koi function...

Fixing the naming to use a safe `fish${id}_` prefix, then defining the pectoral fins with mirrored positioning and orientation for each side, plus starting work on the dorsal fin geometry.

I'm also planning the color palette with orange, white, and red tones for variety, black spheres for eyes, and considering skipping barbels to keep things simple.

Now I'm working out the vector normalization helper and a pine foliage pad function that builds three icosahedron blobs per pad, making sure each call creates fresh geometry rather than sharing instances to avoid mutation issues.
